best_plan.name: p2
best_plan.rationale: p2 wins because it uses the single Movies row for taken_3 and maps the tomatoMeter percentage directly to the positive-review fraction, avoiding 120 per-review LLM sentiment calls. It achieved the best observed quality among tried plans while also being far cheaper and faster than the review-level semantic plans.

cost_model_explanation: I started with a simple prior that treated semantic operators as the main cost driver, then updated it with empirical per-operator cost and latency from observed runs. The traces showed that exact filter/project/groupby operations were nearly free, while review-level sem_map over 120 rows dominated both cost and latency; a one-row sem_map on the movie table was therefore the cheapest and fastest effective strategy.

plan_codes.p1:
pipeline = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name, "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
pipeline.filter(lambda row: str(row.get("idx", "")).strip().lower() == "taken_3")
pipeline.sem_map(
    [{"name": "positive_indicator", "type": int, "description": "Return 1 if the review is overall positive about the movie, else 0."}],
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE,
    depends_on=["reviewText"]
)
pipeline.groupby([], ["average"], ["positive_indicator"])
pipeline.project(["average(positive_indicator)"])
pipeline
plan_codes.p2:
pipeline = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name, "Movies.csv", load_data("Movies.csv"))
pipeline.filter(lambda row: str(row.get("idx", "")).strip().lower() == "taken_3")
pipeline.sem_map(
    [{"name": "positive_fraction", "type": float, "description": "Return the fraction of critic reviews that are positive as a decimal between 0 and 1, based only on the tomatoMeter percentage for this movie."}],
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE,
    depends_on=["tomatoMeter"]
)
pipeline.project(["positive_fraction"])
pipeline
